title: Relative reel performance — planning board
mode: Explain relative performance at the same capture time
status: Planning only; next-step tasks are not executed by creating this board.

notes.title: Explain relative reel performance
notes.text:
Same-capture stats → multiple of the channel baseline.
1× = typical · 1.5× = 50% above · 0.7× = 30% below.
The channel’s absolute view count is not an equation input.
This board is for a descriptive model at the observed capture time.

notes.title: What we have agreed
notes.text:
• Explain performance at the same capture time.
• Show response metrics as percentages.
• Use the channel median as the working baseline.
• Exclude the evaluated reel from its baseline.
Open decision: comparable post ages and formats.

notes.title: Where the prototype stands
notes.text:
• 20 saved reels across 4 channels; 19 aligned model rows.
• Watch % and skip % are the starting inputs.
• Above/below baseline: 13/19 held-out reels correct.
• Median error: 1.61×; always predicting 1×: 1.39×.
The current equation has not beaten the simple benchmark.

notes.title: Ideas worth testing
notes.text:
• Duration may add information lost by percentages.
• Completion × average watch seconds is a candidate interaction.
• Fit the measured curve before assuming constant drop-off.
• Keep first-pass retention and replay-inclusive watch separate.
The old loop-to-views line is not a calibrated predictor.

notes.title: Simone’s remaining gaps
notes.text:
• All 5 saved insight records are recovered.
• Their 5 MP4s are still unavailable locally.
• 2 reels lack viewers; 2 viewer figures are unconfirmed.
• Views are available for all 5.
Media recovery supports X training; viewer recovery supports loop analysis.

notes.title: 1. Freeze the comparison rules
notes.text:
[ ] Define comparable post-age bands and formats.
[ ] Document channel median views as the target baseline.
[ ] Exclude the evaluated reel and flag sparse channel history.
[ ] Specify every percentage denominator.
Done when: one precise row/target definition is written.

notes.title: 2. Audit the 20-reel dataset
notes.text:
[ ] Match every feature to the same capture as its views.
[ ] Add post age and duration where evidence exists.
[ ] Record missing data, rounding, platform and collaboration flags.
[ ] Distinguish actual end retention from the last saved graph point.
Done when: each included value traces to an original source.

notes.title: 3. Build the candidate features
notes.text:
[ ] Keep watch % and skip % as the reference feature set.
[ ] Add duration as context.
[ ] Test true completion × watch % × duration / 10,000.
[ ] Compare early drop-off and later retention where curves exist.
[ ] Label the mathematical coupling in action/view percentages.

notes.title: 4. Fit a small model ladder
notes.text:
[ ] M0: always predict 1×.
[ ] M1: watch % + skip %.
[ ] M2: add duration.
[ ] M3: test the completion/watch interaction.
[ ] Test sharing or saves only with adequate matched coverage.
Keep the model small; estimate new weights from the data.

notes.title: 5. Validate fairly
notes.text:
[ ] Recompute baselines inside each training fold.
[ ] Hold out reels; keep duplicate captures together.
[ ] Also hold out entire channels.
[ ] Compare models on identical eligible reels and folds.
[ ] Report log error, above/below accuracy and error ranges.
Judge magnitude against 1×; direction against a simple class baseline.

notes.title: 6. Keep only demonstrated value
notes.text:
[ ] Check for consistent error improvement over 1×.
[ ] Inspect failures, small-channel instability and breakout misses.
[ ] Retain only features that help held-out results.
[ ] Publish the equation, definitions and an honest error range.
If the gate fails: retain 1× as the benchmark and collect better matched evidence.
